sections.h2: Duplin County Register of Deeds office
sections.html:
Take your deed to 118 Duplin Street in Kenansville. The counter is open Monday to Friday, 8 am to 5 pm. Call 910-296-2108 with questions, send a fax to 910-296-2344, or mail documents to Box 970, Kenansville, NC 28349.

The same staff also take care of:

  • Deeds of trust and powers of attorney.
  • Assumed business names and military records.
  • Maps and plats.
  • Notary commissions and marriage licenses.
  • Certified copies of vital records.

Real property records, vital records and maps can be searched online at duplinrod.com.

Until a deed sits in the public record, its holder has little protection from outsiders. G.S. 47-18 says a deed, contract to convey, option, lease over three years or first-refusal right loses to lien creditors and paying purchasers until it is registered in the county where the land is.

If two documents conflict, the one registered first wins. A signed deed left unfiled exposes the buyer, so find out from your closing attorney when it will be filed.

Ownership data for tax purposes lives with Land Records in the tax department. Call that office after closing to learn when the new owner appears on the account.

Every county uses one statewide fee schedule, G.S. 161-10, and the money is due when you hand in the paper.

What filing costs at the Duplin County office
DocumentFee
Deed or other ordinary instrumentBase $26.00 (15 pages), plus $4.00 each extra page
Deed of trust, mortgageBase $64.00 (35 pages), plus $4.00 each extra page
Plat or map$21.00 for each sheet
Certified copy of a record$5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for the rest, per page
Release of a paid-off deed of trustFree

Two extras come from that statute too: $25.00 on a nonstandard document and $10.00 for each additional instrument in a filing. Pages decide the total, so count them before you mail.

Grantors owe this tax. At one dollar per five hundred dollars of consideration (partial amounts round up), it is collected at the counter before the deed is recorded.

  • The county general fund receives half.
  • The other half is forwarded to the state after the county withholds a 2% collection allowance.
  • A tract spread over several counties pays where most of its value lies.

Your closing attorney can calculate the stamp for your sale price. Without payment, the deed is not accepted.

Two separate buildings, two separate jobs: the register records the deed, and the Tax Department at 117 Beasley Street handles the bill. Reach Collections at 910-296-2112 and assessing at 910-296-2110.

The bill is due September 1 and interest begins January 6, which means an autumn or winter closing comes with an open bill. The tax office refers delinquent accounts to the county attorney. Foreclosure sales are held at the courthouse steps in Kenansville, and the high bidder puts down 20%.

Get a payoff from Collections before closing. Should the parcel lie in Calypso, Greenevers, Kenansville, Magnolia, Rose Hill, Teachey, Wallace or Warsaw, the county collects that town's levy too, and the payoff should include it. The recommended 2026-27 budget sets the county rate at 58 cents per $100, plus fire district rates. Values were last reset January 1, 2025, and the next reset is January 1, 2030.

sections.h2: Steps to get a deed recorded
sections.html:
No document is filed until payment is made, so the order below matters.

  1. Request a payoff from Collections so the year's tax and any back balance are settled at closing.
  2. Have the deed prepared and signed.
  3. Pay the deed stamp and add the page-based fee from the table.
  4. Bring the document to 118 Duplin Street or mail it to Box 970.
  5. When a lender later wants a certified copy, the per-page charge in the table applies.

Selling an inherited house? Decide who may sign for the estate before anything is drafted. The register files paper without ruling on that, so see an attorney and the court clerk first. Cash sales skip the lender's appraisal and underwriting, though recording steps and costs are unchanged.

Yes, they are recorded here, and Chapter 47H adds rules. It covers written agreements for one-to-four family dwellings or manufactured homes priced at $5,000 or more, where the seller keeps title and there are five or more payments after the down payment.

  • Paper, signatures and an acknowledgment are all required.
  • The buyer may rescind up to midnight ending the third business day after execution or delivery.
  • The contract, or a short memorandum of it, must be recorded by the seller within five business days.
  • Forfeiture starts with a written default notice that allows at least 30 days to cure.

A seller who forgets to record loses the protection described above, so put it on the closing checklist.

sections.h2: What to bring when you file
sections.html:
You need the signed, acknowledged deed plus two payments: the page-based fee and the deed stamp. Count pages beforehand. The $26.00 base fee stops at page 15, and the $64.00 deed of trust fee stops at page 35. Every extra page costs $4.00, and a nonstandard layout adds $25.00.

When mailing to Box 970, put everything in one envelope so the clerk can record without calling you back. Not sure whether a second instrument in the same filing triggers the $10.00 charge? Phone 910-296-2108 and ask. Records you want copied later can be ordered from the same counter, so keep the book and page of your recording on file with your closing papers.

Taxes you owe do not vanish when the house sells. They follow the parcel, which is why a closing attorney usually pays them off the top of your proceeds. Delinquent Duplin accounts are referred to the county attorney, and an inherited house with back taxes could already be in line for that. Check with Collections at 910-296-2112 before listing.

Cash buyers sometimes close fast enough to clear the balance before a foreclosure sale date is set. The deed is then recorded, the seller pays the stamp, and the tax account should show the new owner once Land Records catches up.

Duplin County is home to about 51,571 people in 24,235 housing units, 70.3% of them owner-occupied. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $137,400, rent is $865 and household income is $55,148. New building permits totaled 127 in 2025. In-town house or farm acreage, the paperwork goes through that one Kenansville office.

faqs.q: What are the Register of Deeds hours in Duplin County?
faqs.a: The office keeps weekday hours, 8 am to 5 pm, at 118 Duplin Street. Questions go to 910-296-2108.

faqs.q: What will I pay to record a Duplin County deed?
faqs.a: State law sets the fee. A short deed begins at $26.00 and a deed of trust at $64.00, and pages beyond the included count are $4.00 apiece.

faqs.q: Who owes the excise tax on a Duplin County home sale?
faqs.a: The seller. It is paid at the register's counter before recording and works out to one dollar per five hundred dollars of value.

faqs.q: Can I look up Duplin County land records online?
faqs.a: Yes. The register's website, duplinrod.com, has real property records, vital records and maps.

faqs.q: Does recording a deed settle my property tax?
faqs.a: It does not. Tax is billed and collected by the Tax Department and falls due each September 1, so ask Collections for a payoff at 910-296-2112 ahead of closing.
